trust_decision.summary: Whether a Ruby block handed to SQLite as raw user_data for a scalar function stays GC-reachable for as long as SQLite can call it; decided by the @functions retention store, which at the pinned commit is keyed by name only, while SQLite keys functions by (name, arity, text encoding), so a second registration under the same name drops the reference to a block SQLite still holds.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'redefining SQLite functions'; the define_function C body that stores the block keyed by name is the first place anyone looks.

fix_sites.entry_point: SQLite3::Database#initialize (initialises the @functions store the C code writes into)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The second published site (lib/sqlite3/database.rb:178) is the type change for the same store, not a separate route; create_function (lib/sqlite3/database.rb:412-419) is a wrapper but goes through the same C sink, so the single C fix covers it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: None of real weight: every route goes through one C function; the only arguable dismissal is the text-rep variant ('the report only mentions arity') via define_function_with_flags/create_function's text_rep argument.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Overloads by arity/encoding must all stay callable, and a same-name same-arity redefinition must still replace the old block (the new one is used); a fix that rejects redefinition or unregisters the old overload breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: same name, different block arity (incl. -1 splat vs fixed)
same name and arity, different text-rep flags via define_function_with_flags / create_function text_rep (lib/sqlite3/database.rb:412-413)
create_function wrapper path (block wrapped in a new proc, lib/sqlite3/database.rb:413-417)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Collation comparator retention keyed by name; a copy could register collations per text-rep (UTF8/UTF16) while keeping the name-keyed hash, recreating the same mismatch.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: sqlite3_create_collation takes an eTextRep that is hard-coded here (ext/sqlite3/database.c:759); exposing it as a flags argument mirrors define_function_with_flags and a maintainer would naturally keep the existing @collations hash.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Aggregator wrappers were moved to an append-only array by the previous commit; a copy could revert to a name-keyed hash.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same historical pattern as @functions before the fix; but it is a WHERE-type sibling the report would expose.

O9_family: memory safety: use-after-free of a GC-collected callback whose raw pointer is retained by the C library (lifetime/ownership mismatch between Ruby GC and SQLite user_data)

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby with dev headers, C compiler, rake-compiler/mini_portile2; vendored SQLite 3.53.2 tarball fetched from sqlite.org unless pre-cached or built against system libsqlite3 (dependencies.yml:10-13)
O10_build.project_tests: test/test_database.rb (define_function tests), test/test_integration_aggregate.rb:142 (aggregate different-arity overwrite, from sibling fix), minitest via rake test

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Key @functions by [name, arity] (missing the text-rep flag dimension) or by name+arity inside C, instead of retaining every registered block.

out_of_scope_notes: SQLite3::Database#collations is a public attr_reader (lib/sqlite3/database.rb:88); a caller mutating it can drop comparator references — API misuse, not this advisory.
Raw VALUE pointers stored as SQLite user_data (ext/sqlite3/database.c:519, ext/sqlite3/aggregator.c:248) are not pinned against GC.compact; not examined.
Sibling advisory fix for aggregates (commit b24e1e6, #711) is already in the pinned tree (ext/sqlite3/aggregator.c:234-256).
unverified: repo_mb not measured; source is ~6 C files plus Ruby lib, so assumed under 5 MB (tiny_repo).
Whether a prebuilt/cached SQLite tarball is available offline for the build.

Collation route judged safe because eTextRep is fixed to SQLITE_UTF8 (ext/sqlite3/database.c:759) and SQLite replaces by name; case-insensitive / NUL-truncated names only cause over-retention. Not tested.
j_defence_ineffective=1 reflects that a retention store existed (lib/sqlite3/database.rb:178, ext/sqlite3/database.c:527) but failed for differing arity/encoding.
O1 counts define_function, define_function_with_flags and create_function as distinct public calls into the one sink.
